size.footprint: rough estimate ≈ 90–120 m square park inside a perimeter street, plus an annex across the street (apartments, private pool). Not measured.

guidance: The park is a square inside a street and a ring of power lines: the boundary is visible and grindable, so the lap is the obvious line (G3 p059).
Quiksilver banners and flags mark the start and two funboxes; a G3 stat point and a gap (Ghetto Extension) are on the flag.
The spectator platform reads as fragile ("dilapidated", "termites") and invites contact; touching its ladder changes it.
The secret pool is outside the course, across the street, behind a fence that is already broken: the break is the clue (G3 p063).
Every stat-point set puts one point on the power lines (High Wire Act): the overhead ring is the competition's hidden layer.
Remake: cash floats over gaps and slopes; the logo is on a wire above a QP pair, inviting a spine transfer.
designLogic: Competitions have no tape and no letters (G3 p059; PS34 all-tapes list omits Rio). The collectibles are optional (stat points, decks) and sit on or near the scoring lines, so finding them costs time in a judged heat.

The park is built for an endless lap: perimeter rails, short walls, corner guardrails, a bus stop and humps let a skater grind and manual round the course "for combos worth hundreds of thousands of points" (G3 p059, p063).
One loop per layer: the ground lap (rails and walls), the vert loop (pool, spine, roll-ins), and the overhead ring (power lines and red cables).
The only secret area is a deck shrine: all three decks are above the hidden pool across the street. Hiding all the decks in one place rewards one discovery (G3 p064).
An event inside a judged heat: the platform collapse changes the lap mid-competition and adds a wreckage ledge (G3 p060).
Bails cost more than time: the TAS wins with two 3-second heats of one clean combo each (TAS3 2:15-2:30). Judges score points and bails, not exploration.

Gap values grade risk: 500-point gaps are the long airs and high grinds (Over the Platform, Big Tunnel Gap, High Wire Act, Red Line Grind, Take It to da Bridge!), 50-point gaps are small transfers (G3 p065-p068).

Stat points are spread so each skater group explores a different part: trees and planters (Hawk), street-side sitting areas (Caballero), spine and flag (Campbell), platform and pool channel (Glifberg) (G3 p062).

Street furniture as launchers: brick planters, flower-garden borders and a planter slope pop the skater into trees and onto the wires (G3 p062; J3 p014). The competition teaches "pop off a planter" as the way up.

Each stat-point set mixes layers (one or two on the wires, one in a tree or over a planter, one over the pool or a QP, one on the street side), so a single heat can take some without leaving the lap (G3 p062).
The PS1 edition keeps the square-in-a-street plan, the ring of poles and wires and the central pool (VG): the perimeter loop is the part of the design that survived the hardware cut.
remakeChanges: Still a medal competition; no tape or letters added (PS34 rio; PS34 all-tapes list).
Platinum pro goal: Christ Air over the bank by the start (the Over the Bank gap) and place first (PS34).

Added collectibles: cash ×3, hidden deck in the hidden pool (smash rickety boards), Iron Galaxy logo on a wire above a QP pair (spine transfer, catch the wire on the way down), panda in a patio across the road, stat points ×3 (PS34).

PS1 edition (VG): same idea, simpler park: a square park inside a perimeter street with poles and wires, a central oval pool with a long box, planters, a white spectator tent, curved corner rails; the annex across the street is an alley with laundry lines and a stat point; no hidden pool is drawn clearly.
transfer: Hidden yard crystal: across the street from a square park, a walled yard behind a broken fence holds an empty pool; the crystal floats above its deep end, reached by pumping the pool and a vert air of ≈ 4–5 m.

Ring layer: string power lines on poles round the park perimeter at ≈ 4–5 m; the crystal sits on a span between two poles, reached by a kicker or planter-slope launch into a grind snap and held through a corner.
Collapse to reveal: a rickety platform whose ladder breaks when touched drops onto a lower ledge; the wreckage forms a new grindable line that leads to the crystal.
Spine-to-wire catch: two quarter pipes back to back under a wire; spine-transfer and snap onto the wire on the way down (2.1 m snap radius) to ride to a crystal at its end.
openQuestions: Which deck description belongs to which skater group (G3 p064 boxes not fully legible in my reading).
Whether the PS1 edition has a hidden pool (VG shows a dark curved shape near the start but no fence).
